findings.message: decodeSecretKey base64-decodes any value whose length is a multiple of 4 and contains only base64 characters, which corrupts ordinary plain-text credentials. The operator generates 16-char admin passwords from letters+digits+'!@#$%^&*'. About 14% of these, (62/70)^16, are all alphanumeric. Those decode as valid base64 into binary garbage, so the password grant fails with 401. The same happens to any username or password like 'user' or 'abcd1234'.

resolveURL picks status.endpoints.admin/public, which the operator always sets to http://<name>-keycloak.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:8080. That address only resolves inside the cluster, but this CLI runs outside it. A user runs `import-users --keycloak my-kc -n ns --realm r` from a workstation, as the docs show. The token request goes to *.svc.cluster.local and fails DNS resolution. The spec.hostname fallback is never reached, and that field doesn't exist on the CR anyway (the real fields are spec.ingress.host and spec.tls.hostname).

KeycloakSpec.Hostname maps to `spec.hostname`, but the Keycloak CRD has no such field (hostnames live at spec.ingress.host and spec.tls.hostname). The hostname fallback in resolveURL is dead code. A CR with ingress.host=keycloak.example.com but no status endpoints yields an empty URL. The tool errors with 'spec.hostname is not set', telling the user to set a field that doesn't exist.

When importBatch returns an error (HTTP 409/403/5xx, network error, token refresh failure), ImportUsers returns a nil result. The caller's 'print partial result' path prints nothing, and the counts from earlier successful batches are lost. With --mode fail and 3 batches, batch 3 gets a 409. Batches 1-2 were already committed, but the summary is skipped (result==nil), so the operator can't tell how many users were imported.

Keycloak's PartialImportResults JSON has added/skipped/overwritten/results with actions ADDED/SKIPPED/OVERWRITTEN. It has no 'errors' field and no ERROR/FAILED action, so the Errors check is dead and overwritten users are never counted. With --mode overwrite on existing users, Keycloak returns overwritten=N. The summary reports Added: 0, Skipped: 0, which looks like nothing was imported.

The operator accepts the legacy `admin_access` alias for spec.admin (AliasChoices), but the Go struct only reads `admin`. A CR using spec.admin_access.existingSecret=my-secret makes the tool fall back to '<name>-admin-credentials'. That secret doesn't exist, or holds different credentials, so the secret read fails or authentication fails.
